title: DR reflection plan: data-model layer (15 relationship changes)
rationale: Relationship schemas in the data-model layer that the maintainer-note triage and the sorting-question reflection (cli/scripts/spec-enrich) want removed, renamed, reversed or retargeted. Each operation carries the claims and Clef's sorting answers as evidence and the plan's probability. Accepting an operation means DR applies it with apply-walk.ts; rejecting means the schema stays.

operations.rationale: Rename the predicate of data-model.schemadefinition.satisfies.security.dataclassification to data-model.schemadefinition.references.security.dataclassification. Plan kind rename-predicate, p 0.41; claims rel:data-model.schemadefinition#3.

evidence.quote: The satisfies predicate from data-model.schemadefinition to security.dataclassification fits poorly and governed-by or constrained-by would read better. Proposed: Replace the satisfies predicate with governed-by or constrained-by for the link to security.dataclassification.

Sorting answers (rel:data-model.schemadefinition#3): best source of 'satisfies security.dataclassification': data-model.schemadefinition (0.42), data-model.objectschema (0.21), data-model.jsonschema (0.18); best destination of 'data-model.schemadefinition satisfies': security.dataclassification (0.72), motivation.constraint (0.11), none (0.08); best predicate: references (0.41), none (0.22), satisfies (0.13). Outcome: alternative (predicate=references).

operations.rationale: Rename the predicate of data-model.arrayschema.aggregates.data-model.reference to data-model.arrayschema.uses.data-model.reference. Plan kind rename-predicate, p 0.38; claims rel:data-model.arrayschema#1.

evidence.quote: The aggregates relationships from data-model.arrayschema to data-model.reference and to data-model.schemadefinition overlap, because an items $ref is a Reference that resolves to a SchemaDefinition, so both edges may be recorded for a single link. Proposed: Model ArraySchema→Reference and Reference→SchemaDefinition instead of a direct ArraySchema→SchemaDefinition aggregates edge.

Sorting answers (rel:data-model.arrayschema#1): best source of 'aggregates data-model.reference': data-model.arrayschema (0.41), data-model.reference (0.28), data-model.jsonschema (0.16); best destination of 'data-model.arrayschema aggregates': data-model.reference (0.85), data-model.schemadefinition (0.03), data-model.arrayschema (0.03); best predicate: uses (0.38), references (0.21), aggregates (0.14). Outcome: alternative (predicate=uses).

operations.rationale: Rename the predicate of data-model.objectschema.aggregates.data-model.schemaproperty to data-model.objectschema.composes.data-model.schemaproperty. Plan kind rename-predicate, p 0.36; claims node:data-model.objectschema#3.

evidence.quote: The properties attribute on data-model.objectschema duplicates the aggregates relationship to data-model.schemaproperty, so only one representation should exist. Proposed: Keep either the properties attribute or the aggregates relationship to schemaproperty and remove the other.

Sorting answers (node:data-model.objectschema#3): best source of 'aggregates data-model.schemaproperty': data-model.objectschema (0.88), data-model.jsonschema (0.03), data-model.schemaproperty (0.02); best destination of 'data-model.objectschema aggregates': data-model.schemaproperty (0.86), none (0.04), data-model.objectschema (0.02); best predicate: composes (0.36), reverse:references (0.26), aggregates (0.17). Outcome: alternative (predicate=composes).

operations.rationale: Remove data-model.reference.maps-to.api.schema: data-model.schemadefinition.maps-to.api.schema already exists and expresses it. Plan kind retarget, p 0.57; claims rel:data-model.reference#2.

evidence.quote: The relationship data-model.reference maps-to api.schema is less strongly misplaced because it duplicates what the resolved SchemaDefinition would map to. Proposed: Remove or reconsider the maps-to relationship from data-model.reference to api.schema, relying on the mapping of the resolved data-model.schemadefinition.

Sorting answers (rel:data-model.reference#2): best source of 'maps-to api.schema': data-model.schemadefinition (0.57), none (0.14), data-model.reference (0.13); best destination of 'data-model.reference maps-to': api.schema (0.35), none (0.34), api.components (0.24); best predicate: none (0.46), references (0.20), maps-to (0.17). Outcome: alternative (source=data-model.schemadefinition).

evidence.quote: The aggregates relationships from data-model.arrayschema to data-model.reference and to data-model.schemadefinition overlap, because an items $ref is a Reference that resolves to a SchemaDefinition, so both edges may be recorded for a single link. evidence.quote: The realizes relationship from data-model.jsonschema to api.schema could equally be expressed as maps-to. Proposed: Consider changing realizes to maps-to for the relationship to api.schema.

operations.rationale: Retarget of data-model.arrayschema.maps-to.api.response to data-model.jsonschema.maps-to.api.response. Plan kind retarget, p 0.37; claims rel:data-model.arrayschema#2.

evidence.quote: The maps-to relationship from data-model.arrayschema to api.response uses a data-layer predicate, and describing a response body may fit a 'references' or 'used-by' relation better. Proposed: Replace the maps-to predicate with 'references' or 'used-by' for the arrayschema to api.response relationship.

Sorting answers (rel:data-model.arrayschema#2): best source of 'maps-to api.response': data-model.jsonschema (0.37), none (0.35), data-model.arrayschema (0.13); best destination of 'data-model.arrayschema maps-to': api.response (0.79), none (0.13), api.components (0.04); best predicate: none (0.31), maps-to (0.28), references (0.22). Outcome: alternative (source=data-model.jsonschema).

operations.rationale: Retarget of data-model.reference.maps-to.application.applicationservice to data-model.schemadefinition.maps-to.application.applicationservice. Plan kind retarget, p 0.33; claims node:data-model.reference#1, rel:data-model.reference#1.

evidence.quote: The maps-to relationship from data-model.reference to application.applicationservice looks wrong because a schema pointer does not realise a service. Proposed: Remove or replace the maps-to relationship to application.applicationservice.

The relationship data-model.reference maps-to application.applicationservice looks misplaced because a $ref adds no content of its own, so any service mapping belongs on the SchemaDefinition it resolves to. Proposed: Remove the maps-to relationship from data-model.reference to application.applicationservice and place the service mapping on data-model.schemadefinition.

Sorting answers (node:data-model.reference#1): best source of 'maps-to application.applicationservice': data-model.schemadefinition (0.33), none (0.20), data-model.objectschema (0.15); best destination of 'data-model.reference maps-to': none (0.55), application.applicationcomponent (0.14), application.applicationservice (0.12); best predicate: none (0.82), maps-to (0.07), references (0.03). Outcome: alternative (source=data-model.schemadefinition).

Sorting answers (rel:data-model.reference#1): best source of 'maps-to application.applicationservice': data-model.schemadefinition (0.77), data-model.objectschema (0.08), data-model.jsonschema (0.05); best destination of 'data-model.reference maps-to': none (0.35), application.applicationcomponent (0.21), api.schema (0.19); best predicate: none (0.59), maps-to (0.24), realizes (0.04). Outcome: alternative (source=data-model.schemadefinition).

operations.rationale: Retarget of data-model.objectschema.serves.application.applicationfunction to data-model.objectschema.serves.application.applicationservice. Plan kind retarget, p 0.31; claims rel:data-model.objectschema#4.

evidence.quote: The relationships data-model.objectschema serves application.applicationcomponent and data-model.objectschema serves application.applicationfunction are redundant with the inverse of the component's or function's uses or accesses relationship to the object schema. Proposed: Remove the serves relationships and rely on the inverse of the uses or accesses relationships from the application component and function.

Sorting answers (rel:data-model.objectschema#4): best source of 'serves application.applicationfunction': none (0.45), application.applicationservice (0.37), data-store.accesspattern (0.07); best destination of 'data-model.objectschema serves': application.applicationservice (0.31), none (0.26), application.applicationcomponent (0.16); best predicate: none (0.50), references (0.28), serves (0.10). Outcome: alternative (target=application.applicationservice).

operations.rationale: Remove data-model.objectschema.realizes.motivation.goal: data-model.objectschema.realizes.business.businessobject already exists and expresses it. Plan kind retarget, p 0.27; claims rel:data-model.objectschema#1.

evidence.quote: The relationship data-model.objectschema realizes motivation.goal is dubious because data structures rarely realize goals directly; a supports relationship would fit better. Proposed: Replace the realizes relationship to motivation.goal with a supports relationship.

Sorting answers (node:data-model.objectschema#5): best source of 'realizes motivation.goal': none (0.27), application.applicationcomponent (0.17), business.businessprocess (0.16); best destination of 'data-model.objectschema realizes': none (0.38), business.businessobject (0.22), motivation.goal (0.17); best predicate: none (0.88), realizes (0.06), serves (0.01). Outcome: no_better.

Sorting answers (rel:data-model.objectschema#1): best source of 'realizes motivation.goal': none (0.25), business.businessprocess (0.24), application.applicationcomponent (0.14); best destination of 'data-model.objectschema realizes': business.businessobject (0.27), motivation.goal (0.19), application.dataobject (0.19); best predicate: none (0.81), realizes (0.07), references (0.04). evidence.quote: The realizes relationship from data-model.jsonschema to motivation.goal is weak because a data schema rarely realizes a goal directly; a supports/supports-goals predicate fits better. Proposed: Replace realizes with supports (supports-goals) for the relationship to motivation.goal.

operations.rationale: Remove data-model.schemacomposition.composes.data-model.schemadefinition: data-model.schemadefinition.references.data-model.schemadefinition already exists and expresses it. Plan kind compound, p 0.44; claims rel:data-model.schemacomposition#1.

evidence.quote: The 'composes' relationship from data-model.schemacomposition to data-model.schemadefinition is questionable because a named definition exists independently and is reused via $ref, so composition's lifecycle ownership does not fit. Proposed: Replace 'composes' with 'aggregates' or 'references' for the relationship to data-model.schemadefinition.

Sorting answers (rel:data-model.schemacomposition#1): best source of 'composes data-model.schemadefinition': data-model.schemadefinition (0.44), data-model.schemacomposition (0.23), none (0.12); best destination of 'data-model.schemacomposition composes': data-model.schemadefinition (0.56), data-model.reference (0.27), data-model.objectschema (0.05); best predicate: references (0.58), uses (0.20), none (0.07). Outcome: alternative (source=data-model.schemadefinition; predicate=references).

operations.rationale: Change of data-model.jsonschema.serves.application.applicationfunction to application.applicationservice.references.application.applicationfunction. Plan kind compound, p 0.41; claims rel:data-model.jsonschema#3.

evidence.quote: The serves relationships from data-model.jsonschema to application.applicationfunction and business.businessservice are indirect, since passive schemas are accessed rather than serving. Proposed: Replace or reconsider the serves predicate, e.g. use an access-style relationship; none more specific stated.

Sorting answers (rel:data-model.jsonschema#3): best source of 'serves application.applicationfunction': application.applicationservice (0.41), none (0.33), data-model.objectschema (0.08); best destination of 'data-model.jsonschema serves': none (0.43), application.applicationcomponent (0.14), application.applicationfunction (0.13); best predicate: references (0.55), none (0.25), realizes (0.10). Outcome: alternative (source=application.applicationservice; predicate=references).

operations.rationale: Change of data-model.schemaproperty.references.data-model.objectschema to data-model.schemadefinition.aggregates.data-model.schemaproperty. Plan kind compound, p 0.38; claims rel:data-model.schemaproperty#1.

evidence.quote: The five 'references' relationships from data-model.schemaproperty to arrayschema, numericschema, objectschema, schemadefinition and stringschema treat the property's own value subschema as a separate referenced element, although the property has no meaning apart from it, so 'composes' or a typed-by predicate may fit better. Proposed: Replace the 'references' predicate on these five relationships with 'composes' or a typed-by style predicate.

Sorting answers (rel:data-model.schemaproperty#1): best source of 'references data-model.objectschema': data-model.schemaproperty (0.73), data-model.jsonschema (0.12), none (0.10); best destination of 'data-model.schemaproperty references': data-model.schemadefinition (0.40), data-model.objectschema (0.27), data-model.reference (0.14); best predicate: reverse:aggregates (0.38), references (0.32), composes (0.08). Outcome: alternative (target=data-model.schemadefinition; predicate=reverse:aggregates).
